source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: On a rainy evening in Buea, a bowl of hot pepper soup is one of the best things to order. Cooks use soup as a starter to wake up the appetite, as a light meal, and as a way of using bones and vegetable trimmings that might be thrown away. At the GCE you are asked to name the types of soup, to say what goes into a stock, and to describe how a soup is made.

items: Simmering means cooking just below the boiling point, with small bubbles.
Starch thickens a liquid when it is heated in it.
Bones and meat contain flavour and protein that dissolve into hot water.

sections.titre: Soup making: stock, clear and thick soups, and the steps of making a purée soup
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Stock
Stock is the liquid made by simmering bones, meat, fish or vegetables with water, with vegetables and herbs for flavour. It is the base of soups, sauces and gravies. **Suitable foods:** beef, chicken or fish bones, meat and chicken trimmings, and vegetables such as onion, carrot and celery. **Unsuitable foods:** starchy foods such as potato, which cloud the stock, strongly flavoured or green vegetables such as cabbage, and any food that is spoilt.

Rules: start with cold water so that the flavour passes into the liquid; simmer gently and skim off the scum; strain; cool quickly and keep in a refrigerator; remove the fat from the top.

### Types of soup
| Group | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Clear soups | Consommé | a clear soup made from strained, clarified stock; named after its main flavour, for example beef consommé or chicken consommé |
| Clear soups | Broth | a thin soup in which small pieces of meat, vegetables or cereal are left |
| Thick soups | Purée soup | thickened by the sieved or liquidised main ingredient itself; made from pulses (beans, lentils, peas) or from other vegetables |
| Thick soups | Cream soup | a thick soup thickened with flour or cornflour and made with milk or cream |

### Making a purée soup
1. Prepare the vegetables: wash, peel and chop them.
2. Fry the chopped onion gently in a little fat.
3. Add the vegetables or soaked pulses and the stock, and simmer until soft.
4. Rub through a sieve or liquidise.
5. Return to the pan, adjust the thickness with stock or milk, season and reheat.
6. Serve hot in hot bowls with a garnish such as croutons (small pieces of fried or toasted bread) or chopped herbs.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes a soup and asks what it is called.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look for the key words. A clear soup made with a stated meat is a consommé of that meat. A soup of sieved pulse or other vegetables is a purée soup. A soup thickened with a white sauce or flour and milk is a cream soup. A thin soup with pieces left in it is a broth.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked which foods suit stock, or why stock is made.
variantes.contenu_markdown: List suitable foods in separate points: bones, meat trimmings, carcass of a chicken, fish heads and bones for fish stock, onion, carrot and celery. Add that stock makes use of leftovers that would be wasted and gives flavour and food value to soups, sauces and gravy.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked about the place of soup in a meal.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A clear soup is light and stimulates the appetite before a main course. A thick soup with pulses or milk supplies protein and energy and can be a light meal with bread. Hot soup should be served hot, in hot bowls, and cold soup cold.

sections.enonce_markdown: State the difference between a consommé and a purée soup, and describe how a vegetable purée soup is made. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "State" asks for a short difference and "describe" asks for the steps in order. Six marks suggest two for the difference and four for the steps.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part 1: one clear difference. Part 2: about four steps in order.

etapes.justification: Compare both soups on the same point, which is the appearance and thickness.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A consommé is a clear soup made from clarified stock, with no pieces left in it. A purée soup is thick because the sieved or liquidised vegetable thickens it.
Wash, peel and chop the vegetables. Fry chopped onion gently in a little fat, add the vegetables and the stock, and simmer until the vegetables are soft.

etapes.justification: A soup is only complete when it is smooth, seasoned and served well.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Rub the soup through a sieve or liquidise it, return it to the pan, adjust the thickness and season. Reheat and serve hot with a garnish such as croutons.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Difference:** a consommé is clear and thin, made from clarified stock; a purée soup is thick, thickened by the sieved vegetable itself. **Method:** prepare the vegetables, fry the onion, add the vegetables and stock and simmer until soft, sieve or liquidise, season and adjust the thickness, reheat and serve hot with a garnish.

items.erreur_markdown: Naming a clear soup containing beef as a "cream soup".
items.pourquoi_faux: A cream soup is thick and made with milk or cream. A clear soup made from strained meat stock is a consommé.

items.erreur_markdown: Including potato peelings and cabbage leaves among the foods suitable for making clear stock.
items.pourquoi_faux: Starch from potato clouds the stock and cabbage gives a strong, unpleasant flavour.
items.correction_markdown: Use bones, meat trimmings, onion, carrot and celery.

items.erreur_markdown: Putting bones in boiling water and boiling them hard for a short time to make stock.
items.pourquoi_faux: Cold water draws the flavour out of the bones, and hard boiling makes the stock cloudy.
items.correction_markdown: Start with cold water and simmer gently, skimming the scum.

items.erreur_markdown: Leaving stock overnight on the cooker at room temperature.
items.pourquoi_faux: Stock is rich in protein and goes bad quickly, so bacteria multiply in it.
items.correction_markdown: Cool it quickly, strain it and keep it in a refrigerator.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing a purée soup without the step of sieving or liquidising.
items.pourquoi_faux: This step makes the soup smooth and thick.
items.correction_markdown: Include rubbing through a sieve or liquidising.

items.enonce_markdown: Name each soup: (a) a clear soup made from clarified chicken stock; (b) a thick soup made from sieved lentils; (c) a thin soup in which small pieces of meat and vegetables are left; (d) a soup thickened with flour and milk.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Chicken consommé.** (b) **Purée soup** (a pulse purée soup). (c) **Broth.** (d) **Cream soup.**

items.enonce_markdown: A cook makes 6 litres of soup and serves it in portions of 300 ml. (a) How many portions are served? (b) Each portion is sold at 500 FCFA. Find the total sales. (c) The ingredients cost $4\,000$ FCFA. Find the profit. (Use 1 litre = 1,000 ml.)

A cook has these items: chicken bones, carrot peelings, celery leaves, potato peelings, cabbage leaves and some meat that smells bad. (a) Choose the items suitable for making stock and give a reason for rejecting each of the others. (b) Describe how the stock should be made and stored. (c) Name two uses of the stock.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Suitable: **chicken bones, carrot peelings, celery leaves**. Rejected: potato peelings, because the starch makes the stock cloudy; cabbage leaves, because they give a strong flavour; the meat that smells bad, because it is spoilt and unsafe. (b) Put the bones and vegetables in cold water, bring slowly to a simmer, skim off the scum, simmer gently, then strain. Cool quickly, remove the fat and keep it in a refrigerator. (c) Any two of: soups, sauces, gravy, stews and cooking rice or vegetables for flavour.

items_markdown: Stock is made by simmering bones, meat trimmings and vegetables such as onion, carrot and celery in water; avoid potato, cabbage and spoilt food.
Make stock from cold water, simmer gently, skim, strain, cool quickly and keep it cold.
Clear soups: consommé (clarified stock, named after its meat, for example beef consommé) and broth (pieces left in).
Thick soups: purée soups (thickened by sieved pulses or other vegetables) and cream soups (flour and milk or cream).
To make a purée soup: prepare, fry the onion, simmer with stock, sieve or liquidise, season and adjust, reheat and garnish.
Serve hot soup hot in hot bowls; soup stimulates the appetite as a starter and uses leftovers.
